newsitem.title: USA: Western launches $3.5 billion bid for ADT.
newsitem.headline: Western launches $3.5 billion bid for ADT.

text.p: Western Resources Inc. said Wednesday it bid $3.5 billion to buy the rest of ADT Ltd, the largest electronic security firm in North America.

The offer follows Republic Industries Inc.'s failed $5 billion bid to take over ADT in September, which was terminated due to a sharp drop in Republic's share price that lowered the value of the proposed merger.
Western Resources, an energy and security services company based in Topeka, Kan., currently holds about 27 percent of ADT.

The acquisition would be Western's second in the security business this week. Western said Monday it agreed to buy Westinghouse Electric Corp.'s monitored security services business for $368 million in cash.

It is offering $22.50 for each share of ADT, consisting of $15 in Western Resources common stock and $7.50 cash. The deal gives ADT holders a 12 percent premium over Tuesday's closing stock price of $20.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Western also said the deal would give ADT shareholders a dividend, which they currently do not receive, of about 99 cents a share based on the shares of Western Resources they would acquire in the proposed transaction.

Western Resources said it is calling for a special meeting of ADT shareowners to replace ADT's board of directors to complete the transaction. The offer will be made directly to ADT shareowners through an exchange offer Western Resources intends to file shortly, it said.
